children: Shares of InnovAge fell after the healthcare company said funds affiliated with Apax Partners and Welsh, Carson, Anderson & Stowe would sell 10 million shares in a secondary offering.
Shares were down 13% to $9.30 in after-hours trading on Tuesday. The stock closed up 0.5% at $10.66, and has more than doubled in value this year.
The company said underwriters for the offering will have a 30-day option to buy an additional 1.5 million shares at the offering price.
InnovAge said it isn't offering any shares and won't receive any proceeds from the offering.
